value.body: Research analysts collect and analyse data on a sector, market, company or policy topic and write up what they find. They work in equity and market research firms, consulting and knowledge-process outsourcing companies, think tanks and policy organisations, and their day mixes data work, reading and writing reports.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BA / B.Sc in Economics or Statistics, B.Com; often a master's

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Excel, a statistics package (R, Stata or Python), databases

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers often start as junior or associate analysts in research-outsourcing and market-research firms, or as research assistants at think tanks. A master's degree in economics or statistics, or a certification such as NISM Research Analyst for equity research, widens the options.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Finding and cleaning data from public and paid sources
Reading reports and policy documents critically

value.title: At a glance
items: Equity research roles require NISM Research Analyst certification under SEBI rules.
Common next steps: senior analyst, consultant, or a move into data or policy roles.
Policy and think-tank roles often favour a master's degree.
